Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Did the Quran foretell one man's unbelief?

A chapter names a living man and says he will not believe. He had years to disprove it. Prediction or curse?

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ١ مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ٢ سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.[2008] His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained. He will [enter to] burn in a Fire of [blazing] flame

Translator's notes

[2008] Abū Lahab (the Prophet's uncle) , who was an enemy of Islām.

Quran · Al-Masad 111:1-3

Translation

Riches don’t profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־יוֹעִ֣יל ה֭וֹן בְּי֣וֹם עֶבְרָ֑ה וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת׃

Proverbs · 11:4

World English Bible

Most prophecy is about nobody in particular. This chapter names one man, by his nickname, while he is alive. It says his wealth will not save him and that his end will be hard. Scholars read this as saying he would die without believing. Then the test is simple, and it was in his own hands: a spoken word of belief would have made the chapter look wrong. Nobody was stopping him.

A question for you

What would make a statement like this a fair test of itself?

If you sayThat it names a person and a choice they can make.
ThenThat is the shape of this one: the man could have changed the outcome by a spoken word.
If you sayThat it can be checked afterwards.
ThenIt can, from the sources, with the limits noted here.
If you sayThat it is specific.
ThenIt is specific about the person and silent about the date, which is part of what scholars debate.

Part 2 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ١ مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.[2008] His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained.

Translator's notes

[2008] Abū Lahab (the Prophet's uncle) , who was an enemy of Islām.

Quran · Al-Masad 111:1-2

Now the objections, fairly. First, the opening word can be read as a curse, ‘may his hands perish’, not a forecast. Second, a man who opposed the message for years was a safe bet not to change. The reply: many early opponents did change, so the bet was not free of risk, and a pretended conversion by this named, living man would have undone the chapter. The risk ran one way.

A question for you

How do you read the opening word of the chapter?

If you sayAs a forecast.
ThenThen the question is how risky it was, and the ‘safe bet’ objection is the thing to weigh.
If you sayAs a curse.
ThenThat is a serious reading, and it weakens the case. The text is then strong feeling rather than a forecast, and this Step would not count it as a sign.
If you sayI cannot tell.
ThenUnderstandable. Scholars of Arabic read it both ways. Hold it open.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

One more thing keeps this in proportion. The book that names this man also tells every reader, whatever they have done, not to despair of mercy. The chapter is not a model for how to think about anyone alive today. It is a single case, in a single life, in the Quran's own account. What it offers a reader is a test the book set against itself, not a verdict on anyone alive today.

A question for you

What does it mean to you that the same book holds both?

If you sayThat the chapter is a test, not a verdict on people today.
ThenThat is the reading this Step takes.
If you sayThat they pull in different directions.
ThenThey can seem to. Scholars have written on how the two fit, and you can read them. This Step does not claim to settle it.
If you sayI want to read the whole chapter first.
ThenFair. It is five verses. Read it slowly and see for yourself.
